text:
COP rose modestly today, continuing a choppy week that started with a steeper decline. The stock has recovered slightly after dropping to $129.52 on August 27th, likely supported by oil prices holding above $83 per barrel and by geopolitical tension in the Middle East — specifically U.S. military strikes on Iranian positions over the weekend, which heightened concerns about potential supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed global oil prices up more than 1% on Monday.

The broader backdrop matters here: escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and tightening financial sanctions on Iran-linked entities (Treasury moving against Egyptian bank branches, new restrictions on dollar use) create genuine uncertainty about crude supplies flowing through one of the world's most critical shipping chokepoints. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, geopolitical risk that threatens global supply typically supports prices, even as it adds volatility.
